title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon and moved swiftly through their agenda and are making way for many activities in the coming weeks.

Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order and recognized visitors.  Chris Schoo with Louisville American Legion Post #914 presented a plaque to Mayor Spicer in honor of the City of Flora’s support of the “Be the One Walk,” the effort to call attention to the problem of Veteran suicide in America.  Schoo thanked them and encouraged everyone to join them and Flora American Legion Post #14 and participate in the third march from Flora to Louisville this Saturday, March 9 at 8:00am starting at the World War II Memorial at Flora’s Library Park and ending at the Veterans Memorial at the Clay County Courthouse in Louisville.  Lunch is served at the Louisville American Legion following the event and participants will be taken back to Flora afterwards.  It is reported that 6,000 Veterans take their own each year in the United States.  Mayor Spicer thanked Schoo for the award and implores everyone to join them and wishes them success in their effort.

Next, Kristen Logan with the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders addressed commissioners seeking their approval of the use of the Clay County Fairgrounds for their annual Crain-Scates Bucking Bulls Rodeo.  The event is planned for Friday, July 24 at 7:00pm to kick off the 2026 Clay County Fair and features not only Bull Riding, but also Barrel Racing, Mutton Busting, the popular Rodeo Clown and the Bit Drill Team.  Logan noted the pre-sale tickets are $12 and $15 at the gate.  Kids 5 and under are admitted free.  She also assured the council that everything is pretty much the same as in previous years and their insurance is up to date.  They are encouraged by the increasing popularity of the event and their attendance numbers have been good.  She also stated that the Clay County 4H Barbecue will take place the same day from 4:00-7:00pm at the REA Building.  Commissioners quickly approved Logan’s request.

Flora’s Superintendent of Public Services Toby Rinehart filled in for former commissioner Mike Genthe to represent the Clay County Cruisers Car Club.  Rinehart explained the club is requesting to use Charley Brown Park for their 22nd Annual Car and Truck Show on Saturday, July 25 from 9:00am-2:00pm.  Rinehart earned unanimous approval for the event.

Mayor Spicer then asked and received approval of the meeting agenda and the consent agenda.  The latter included past meeting and hearing minutes and the April warrant list.

In regular business, Mayor Spicer thanked the Flora Rotary Club for installing the new bathrooms at the Pickleball Courts which she adds are now open.  The mayor also thanked the Flora Coon Hunters Club for their events hosted at Charley Brown Park.  She added that City Administrator Mike Stanford paid a visit to the hunters during their recent event and the club presented him with a plaque, thanking the City of Flora for its support.  Mayor Spicer noted the coon hunters love coming to Flora and they bring many visitors to our community, and in turn, they spend not only their time in Flora, but also their dollars.  She also encouraged residents to get ready for Spring Clean Up coming May 18.  Details are available on the city website, florail.govoffice2.com.  It also includes B & H Recycling returning to town on Saturday May 16 from 9:00-11:00am at the old Clay Medical building just off E. North Ave. in downtown Flora.

Next, Mayor Spicer asked and commissioners approved naming Maralee Johnson, Robbin Dickey and Joe McCoy to the Flora Public Library Board of Trustees for a three-year term that ends April 30, 2029.  They also approved naming Jane Blanchette to the Flora Public Library Board of Trustees to complete the term of Karen Briscoe, which ends April 30, 2027.  Council members also ratified the resignation of Debbie Lamb from the Flora Tourism Committee, effective April 19.

In polling commissioners for their comments, Jeremy Henderson took a moment to congratulate all graduates for their accomplishment.  Other commissioners echoed Henderson’s sentiments.  Commissioner Phil Wiley commented on the number of activities quickly approaching, including Springfest on Saturday, May 16 at Flora’s Library Park.  The Barbecue Cook Off will feature many participants as well as other vendors and merchants offering spring products for sale such as patio furniture.  There are also lawn games and inflatables for the kids.  Don’t forget about the 10th Annual 6K Walk for Water at 9:00am at First Christian Church of Flora.  Wiley also presented a resolution to adopt the revised Net Metering Policy for 2026, and the measure was approved without dissent.  Commissioner Lacey Lewis added to Wiley’s list of upcoming activities.  She said that Flora Tourism is hosting a fundraiser at St. Stephen’s Church to help pay for this year’s Flora fireworks display.  Salt and Strings Butchery is offering a curbside pork steak dinner with potato salad, baked beans, roll and dessert for $15.  Drive-thru serving runs from 4:00-7:00pm.  Tickets are available from Lacey Lewis, Phil Wiley, Ted Whitehead or any Tourism Committee member, the Flora Chamber of Commerce or at Salt and Strings.

Flora City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford again noted the recycling event is coming up Saturday, May 16 from 9:00-11:00am and will accept a laundry list of items.  Details are available on the city website.  He also noted that B & H Recycling now charges for the items they accept.

Stanford also presented an ordinance approving the awarding of the bid and sale of the property at 121 W. Maple St. to Anthony Booth for $2,000.  Commissioners approved the measure unanimously.

Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles stated that the Flora Swimming Pool is on schedule to open on Saturday, May 23.

title: LOUISVILLE VILLAGE BOARD SPECIAL MEETING
full_story:
The Louisville Village Board met Monday evening in special session to take action on their FY2027 Budget.

Prior to the meeting, a budget public hearing was held.  With no public comment, the hearing ended and the special meeting got underway.

Mayor Chris Rinehart called the meeting to order, with trustees quickly approving the meeting agenda and past meeting minutes.

Trustees then briefly examined the proposed FY2027 budget and a motion was then made to approve it.  The board approved the budget on a unanimous vote.

Next, the mayor asked the board to consider approving the prevailing wage.  After a brief discussion, members approved the measure without dissent.

Mayor Rinehart then began a discussion concerning the façade improvement grant program.  He said when the program began several years ago, the reimbursement was capped at $2,500.  Business owners paid for their improvements and the village reimbursed them for half of the amount up to the $2,500 cap, a few years later, the cap was increased to $5,000 and Rinehart asked trustees if they believed as he did that the cap needs to be raised again and suggested a cap of $10,000.  With no one objecting, a vote was taken and it was approved unanimously 6-0.

During open time, the freewheeling discussion included topics of how to use the monies from the TIF fund which total around $280,000 and from the Louisville Business District of around $110,000.  Ideas included using the money for improvements to village streets, perhaps authorizing higher amounts to assist businesses, installing fencing around the water tower and replacing old fencing near Nancy Byers property, making improvements to the K-1 building since Headstart is looking to add another classroom.  The village uses one classroom for storage and will have to move items out and make other improvements including painting, fixing ceiling tiles and waxing floors.  Additional parking space is needed and repairs to the sidewalk may be taken up too.  Repairs at other buildings may be considered too.  Mayor Rinehart also suggested a contest for Louisville residents for America’s 250th Birthday.  Residents would decorate their property and the winner would receive a prize of utility bill credit, with the amount to be determined.  He also thought the village might also run a similar contest in December.  There is also a request for repairs or changes to be made to Broadway St. and Utilities Superintendent Troy Elwood said there is a plan for Broadway and it will be considered at a future meeting.

No action was taken on any item during open time.  With all business completed, the meeting adjourned.

title: SEEKING BIDS
full_story:
Clay County is seeking sealed bids for a used 2016 Ford Utility Interceptor.  Proposal forms are available at the Sheriff’s Office.  This vehicle may be viewed and inspected at the Clay County Sheriff’s Office at 300 Broadway Louisville.

Proposals are to be placed in a sealed envelope marked “2016 Ford Utility Interceptor” and submitted no later than 1:00 pm on May 8th, to the Clay County Sheriff’s Office 300 Broadway/P.O. Box 267 Louisville, IL 62858, at which time all bids will be opened and publicly read aloud.  Sale is subject to County Board approval on May 12th, at 6:00pm.

Equipment is to be sold as is and where is.  Successful bidder shall furnish a bank draft or cashier’s check in the full amount of the bid upon taking possession of equipment no later than May 15th.

The Ford Interceptor has 184,784 miles on it, a 3.7 liter Engine.  This vehicle was used as a patrol unit until April 2026.  This vehicle has motor and transmission issues and is being sold as is.

The County reserves the right to reject any and all bids and to select and award to the bidder whose bid it is felt is in the best interest of the County.

title: PLUMMER HONORS RIDGLEY
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer announced the passage of Senate Joint Resolution 53, honoring the life and sacrifice of US Army Sergeant Kenneth Levi Ridgley of Olney.

The resolution designates US Highway 50 from the intersection of US Highway 50 and Illinois Route 130 in Olney to 10 miles west of Olney as the “Sgt. Levi Ridgley Memorial Highway.”

“Sgt. Levi Ridgley gave his life serving our country, and this designation ensures his courage and sacrifice will always be remembered,” said Senator Plummer.  “It is an honor to help recognize a hometown hero whose dedication to our nation reflected the very best of Illinois.”

A native of Olney, Sgt. Ridgley had long aspired to serve in the military.  He was remembered not only for his service, but also for his deep ties to family and community.  He left behind his wife, Charity, and was in the process of adopting her 3-year-old son, Dillon.

Before enlisting in the US Army, Sgt. Ridgley served six years in the Illinois National Guard, which helped support his education at Southern Illinois University.  While at SIU, he was a member of the rodeo team.  He later left college to become a blacksmith and went on to work in Colorado as a wrangler and horseshoer.

Sgt. Ridgley later enlisted in the US Army and was assigned to the 3rd Battalion, 21st Infantry Regiment, 1st Brigade, 25th Infantry Division, Stryker Brigade Combat Team, at Fort Lewis, Washington.

On March 30th of 2005, Sgt. Ridgley was killed in action during Operation Iraqi Freedom when gunfire erupted at a checkpoint as US soldiers prepared to inspect a vehicle.

“Sgt. Ridgley was a true hero and this memorial highway will stand as a lasting tribute to Sgt. Ridgley’s bravery, service, and sacrifice,” said Senator Plummer.  “It will also serve as a reminder to future generations of the tremendous cost of the freedoms we enjoy every day.”

Senate Joint Resolution 53 unanimously passed out of the Senate and now heads to the House for further consideration.

title: IPRB ENROLLMENT OPEN
full_story:
IPRB still has several openings for their annual Illinois math and science summer teachers program, to be held June 23rd through 26th in Mt. Vernon.  Illinois grade 3 through 12 math and science teachers are eligible to attend.

Teachers who complete the program will receive 37 1/2 professional development hours.  Teachers will get a grade specific classroom activity kit that can be used to teach lessons from a printed Illinois State Board of Education-approved curriculum.  And real-world insight into the Illinois oil production industry via an Illinois oil production site field trip and instruction from numerous industry professionals.

title: FLORA CLEAN-UP DAYS
full_story:
The City of Flora will have town-wide clean-up days May 18th through the 22nd.

Accumulated, unwanted items at residences will be picked up at no extra charge on the residents normal trash day.  It is requested small or loose items should be bundled or bagged.  Carpet needs to be cut and tied so one person can handle it, broken glass items need to be bagged and marked for safety, multiple items such as brooms, mops, blinds, etc. need to be tied together, pool liners need to be cut down, and metal swing sets need to be broken down.  All mattresses and box springs must be wrapped in plastic, in order to be picked up.

For electronic items such as televisions and monitors, radios, tape recorders, computer hard drives, monitors, printers, cell phones, etc. residents are ask to please contact Secure Processors at 618-662-4823.

Republic Services, Flora’s solid waste hauler, will not accept any white goods such as stoves, dishwashers, washing machines, clothes dryers, etc., tires or vehicle/boat parts, paint, hazardous materials/waste, landscape waste, construction/remodeling/demolition materials, concrete/brick/asphalt, batteries, pressurized tanks, gas/oil/antifreeze, ammunition, or explosives.

Residents may deliver their properly decommissioned, no Freon or Oil, white goods to Public Works West lot at 200 Fairview Street.  Please follow the signs posted.  This will be a residential only pick up site.  The city will only be accepting white goods daily between the hours of 7:30 am to 3:30 pm.

Please keep weight in mind when grouping items, such as books and magazines, in a bag or trash container.

Residents with any further questions should call 618-662-4625 or email [email protected].

title: CHAMBER GOLF SCRAMBLE
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce is now accepting sponsorships for their 28th annual golf scramble to be held on Friday, June 5th.

The Chamber offers a variety of sponsorship opportunities to suit every budget.  From Gold Sponsorship at $400 to the affordable Bronze Sponsorship at $50, there’s an option for everyone to get involved and showcase their support for the Flora business community.

Team registration is $50 per person or $200 per team.  Entry fee includes 4 drink tickets courtesy of the Flora Bank and Trust a goodie bag with a sleeve of balls and lunch courtesy of the Flora Savings Bank.  There will also be mulligans, 4 foot strings, yellow tee boxes, for $20 each or $50 for all 3.

Check-in will begin at 11:30 am inside the Clubhouse, lunch is at Noon, and tee-time at 1:00pm.

To register your team call Arriel Dulaney at the Flora Chamber of Commerce at 618-662-5646.

title: UNEMPLOYMENT IN STATE UP
full_story:
The Illinois unemployment rate in March was 5.1%, up from an even 5% in February and up from 4.6% in March 2025.

Total nonfarm payrolls increased over-the-month in March, up 8,400.

The industry sectors with the largest monthly payroll jobs increases include Private Education and Health Services, Professional and Business Services, and Government.  The industry sectors with the largest over-the-month job decreases included Trade, Transportation and Utilities, Financial Activities, and Manufacturing.

Compared to a year ago, total nonfarm payroll jobs were down 4,300.
